es.summary: La cirrosis hepática es la sustitución del tejido hepático sano por fibrosis, provocando pérdida de función y complicaciones sistémicas.
key_points: Fibrosis irreversible que reduce la síntesis de proteínas y coagulación.
Hipertensión portal genera ascitis, varices y sangrado.
Complicaciones principales: encefalopatía, insuficiencia renal y carcinoma hepatocelular.
El tratamiento se centra en la causa, control de líquidos y prevención de hemorragias.

pathophysiology: Daño hepático crónico → necrosis de hepatocitos.
Activación de células estrelladas → depósito de colágeno.
Formación de nódulos regenerativos rodeados de fibrosis.
Obstrucción del flujo portal → hipertensión portal.
Disminución de la función sintética y detoxificante.
signs_symptoms: Ictericia y color amarillento de la piel.
Ascitis y edema de miembros inferiores.
Varices esofágicas o gástricas con riesgo de sangrado.
Confusión o asterixis por encefalopatía hepática.
diagnostics: Albúmina ↓ y tiempo de protrombina prolongado.
Ecografía abdominal con elastografía muestra fibrosis.
Tomografía o resonancia para detectar varices y tumor.
Biopsia hepática (cuando es necesaria) confirma cirrosis.
treatment: Abstinencia total de alcohol y tratamiento antiviral si corresponde.
Diuréticos de asa (furosemida) y antagonistas de aldosterona (espironolactona).
Betabloqueantes no selectivos para prevenir ruptura de varices.
nursing_care: Valoración diaria de peso, circunferencia abdominal y edema.
Monitoreo de signos vitales, especialmente presión arterial y frecuencia respiratoria.
Control de nivel de conciencia y presencia de asterixis.
Administración y evaluación de respuesta a diuréticos.
Prevención de infecciones y cuidado de la piel para evitar úlceras.
patient_teaching: Dieta baja en sodio (<2 g/día) y evitar alimentos procesados.
Abstinencia total de alcohol y cumplimiento del tratamiento antiviral.
Reconocer signos de sangrado (hematemesis, melena) y acudir al servicio de urgencias.
Importancia de la adherencia a diuréticos y suplementos de potasio.
Programar controles de laboratorio y ecografías periódicas.

evidenced_by: ascitis con aumento de circunferencia abdominal
outcomes: Reducción del edema periférico en 48 h
Disminución de la circunferencia abdominal en 2 cm en 5 días

interventions.action: Medir peso y circunferencia abdominal cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Permite evaluar la respuesta al tratamiento diurético.

interventions.action: Administrar furosemida y espironolactona según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Promueven la excreción de sodio y agua, reduciendo la ascitis.

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada turno
interventions.rationale: Facilita el cálculo del balance hídrico.

interventions.action: Elevar extremidades inferiores cuando sea seguro
interventions.rationale: Ayuda a disminuir el edema periférico por gravedad.

interventions.action: Evaluar presencia de crepitación pulmonar y dificultad respiratoria
interventions.rationale: Detecta edema pulmonar temprano.

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar electrolitos séricos cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta alteraciones tempranas y guía el ajuste de diuréticos.

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de potasio oral o IV según indicación
interventions.rationale: Previene hipocalemia asociada a furosemida.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente una dieta rica en potasio (plátano, papaya, aguacate)
interventions.rationale: Apoya la reposición natural de potasio.

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de hiponatremia (confusión, cefalea) y hiperkalemia (debilidad muscular)
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención rápida antes de complicaciones graves.

interventions.action: Ajustar la dosis de diuréticos en coordinación con el médico según resultados de laboratorio
interventions.rationale: Mantiene el equilibrio electrolítico y evita sobre‑diuresis.

en.summary: Hepatic cirrhosis is the replacement of healthy liver tissue with fibrosis, leading to loss of function and systemic complications.
key_points: Irreversible fibrosis that reduces protein synthesis and coagulation.
Portal hypertension causes ascites, varices, and bleeding.
Main complications: encephalopathy, renal failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma.
Treatment focuses on the cause, fluid control, and bleeding prevention.

pathophysiology: Activation of stellate cells → collagen deposition.
Formation of regenerative nodules surrounded by fibrosis.
Obstruction of portal flow → portal hypertension.
signs_symptoms: Jaundice and yellowing of the skin.
Esophageal or gastric varices with bleeding risk.
Confusion or asterixis from hepatic encephalopathy.
diagnostics: Abdominal ultrasound with elastography shows fibrosis.
CT or MRI to detect varices and tumors.
treatment: Total alcohol abstinence and antiviral therapy if indicated.
Non‑selective beta‑blockers to prevent variceal rupture.
nursing_care: Daily assessment of weight, abdominal circumference, and edema.
Monitor vital signs, especially blood pressure and respiratory rate.
Assess level of consciousness and presence of asterixis.
Administer and evaluate response to diuretics.
Prevent infections and skin care to avoid ulcers.
patient_teaching: Low‑sodium diet (<2 g/day) and avoid processed foods.
Total alcohol abstinence and adherence to antiviral treatment.
Recognize signs of bleeding (hematemesis, melena) and seek emergency care.
Importance of adherence to diuretics and potassium supplements.
Schedule regular lab tests and ultrasounds.

outcomes: Reduction of peripheral edema within 48 h
↓ abdominal circumference by 2 cm in 5 days

interventions.action: Measure weight and abdominal circumference every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Allows assessment of diuretic response.

interventions.action: Administer furosemide and spironolactone as prescribed
interventions.rationale: Promote sodium and water excretion, reducing ascites.

interventions.action: Record intake and output each shift
interventions.rationale: Facilitates calculation of fluid balance.

interventions.action: Elevate lower extremities when safe
interventions.rationale: Helps reduce peripheral edema by gravity.

interventions.action: Assess for pulmonary crackles and respiratory distress
interventions.rationale: Detects early pulmonary edema.

interventions.action: Obtain and record serum electrolytes every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detects early changes and guides diuretic adjustment.

interventions.action: Administer oral or IV potassium supplements as indicated
interventions.rationale: Prevents hypokalemia associated with furosemide.

interventions.action: Teach patient a potassium‑rich diet (banana, papaya, avocado)
interventions.rationale: Supports natural potassium replenishment.

interventions.action: Assess signs of hyponatremia (confusion, headache) and hyperkalemia (muscle weakness)
interventions.rationale: Allows prompt intervention before serious complications.

interventions.action: Adjust diuretic dose in coordination with the physician based on lab results
interventions.rationale: Maintains electrolyte balance and avoids over‑diuresis.

sources.name: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Hepatic and Biliary Disorders

summary.0.quote: Cirrhosis is scarring of the liver.

key_points.1.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

key_points.2.quote: Common complications seen with chronic liver disease are esophageal varices , hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome (kidney dysfunction in patients with advanced liver disease), and hepatocellular carcinoma.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: Portal Hypertension Another liver condition, portal hypertension , is an increase in pressure within the portal venous system because of resistance to portal blood flow.

sections.pathophysiology.4.quote: Liver function tests may show increased alanine transaminase (ALT) level and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, bilirubin and prothrombin times will be increased, and albumin level decreased.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: In the United States, the most common causes are chronic alcoholism and hepatitis .

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Causes of cirrhosis include alcohol-induced hepatitis from chronic heavy alcohol use autoimmune diseases, such as autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, or primary sclerosing cholangitis cardiovascular disease, such as congestive heart failure

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Jaundice occurs when skin and sclera (whites of the eyes) ( Figure 19.17 ) turn yellow as a result of too much bilirubin in the body.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Cirrhosis can lead to : Easy bruising or bleeding, or nosebleeds Swelling of the abdomen or legs Extra sensitivity to medicines High blood pressure in the vein entering the liver Enlarged veins called varices in the esophagus and stomach.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Blood ammonia levels may be elevated, indicating hepatic encephalopathy ( Table 19.10 ).

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: Liver function tests may show increased alanine transaminase (ALT) level and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, bilirubin and prothrombin times will be increased, and albumin level decreased.

sections.diagnostics.4.quote: A liver biopsy can confirm chronic liver disease.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Other specific treatments include viral suppression for viral hepatitis ; alcohol abstinence; treatment of metabolic syndromes; identification and cessation of use of drugs or toxins; and immunosuppression and prescription of corticosteroids for autoimmune disorders.

sections.treatment.4.quote: The Model of End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) Score is used to predict survival of patients with cirrhosis and is a tool used to prioritize organ allocation for liver transplantation.

sections.complications.0.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.complications.2.quote: Common complications seen with chronic liver disease are esophageal varices , hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome (kidney dysfunction in patients with advanced liver disease), and hepatocellular carcinoma.

sections.complications.3.quote: Common complications seen with chronic liver disease are esophageal varices , hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome (kidney dysfunction in patients with advanced liver disease), and hepatocellular carcinoma.

sections.complications.4.quote: The bleeding at a venipuncture site followed by oozing of blood from every site or orifice available could indicate coagulopathy, such as disseminated intravascular coagulation.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: These include administering medications documenting daily weights and abdominal girth measurement educating patients monitoring laboratory values, such as sodium levels monitoring vital signs and intake and output

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: The patient will need frequent assessments of respiratory status and fluid and electrolytes status.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Asterixis, or flapping movements, when the patient holds out the arms Hyperreflexia Muscle twitching Cognitive impairment Anxiety or irritability Balance or coordination problems Diagnosis Confirm liver disease.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Double the dose as needed until the desired diuretic response is attained, not to exceed 40 mg.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: The patient must know when to call the provider, signs and symptoms of an infection, organ rejection, lymph node enlargement, and skin changes.
